subcategory: graph-based RAG with flow-based pruning of relational paths and path-based prompting
task: Query-focused, open-ended question answering over large text collections
problem: Graph-based RAG (GraphRAG, LightRAG) retrieves redundant rather than insufficient information and places it in prompts as a flat list, which hurts answer quality.
architecture: PathRAG: an indexing graph is built as in GraphRAG; node retrieval matches LLM-extracted query keywords to nodes by embedding similarity; a distance-aware flow-based pruning algorithm (resource propagation with decay alpha) extracts key relational paths between retrieved nodes; paths are converted to text and ordered in a path-based prompt for the LLM.
retriever: text-embedding-3-small keyword-to-node matching + flow-based path pruning (N = 40, K = 15)
knowledge_source: entity-relation indexing graph built from the text corpus

datasets.name: UltraDomain
datasets.details: Agriculture, CS, Legal, History, Biology, Mix subsets

metrics: LLM-judged win rate (comprehensiveness, diversity, logicality, relevance, coherence)
key_results: Average win rates of 59.93% against GraphRAG and 57.09% against LightRAG across six datasets.
Average win rate of 62.52% in comprehensiveness and 65.37% in diversity against all baselines.
Uses 14,438 tokens per query vs 16,728 for LightRAG (13.69% fewer); the light version PathRAG-lt uses 9,968.
strengths: Shows that pruning redundant graph context and ordering it as paths improves answers while reducing tokens.
Robustness checks under graph sparsity and with three different base/evaluator LLMs; ten trials averaged.

limitations.text: No ground-truth answers: evaluation relies on LLM-judged pairwise win rates.
Indexing graph construction is inherited from GraphRAG and its cost is not reduced; the authors plan to optimise it and to collect more human-annotated data.

title: PathRAG: Pruning Graph-based Retrieval Augmented Generation with Relational Paths
